transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess what brings me in is I’ve just been really hard on myself lately. Like, I keep thinking I’m not actually “senior” material at work, even though they gave me more responsibility, and maybe I somehow fooled everyone into thinking I can handle it.

It’s funny, not funny, but in computer systems there’s always someone who knows the thing faster than you, and I’ll get stuck comparing myself to them instead of just doing the job. Anyway… that’s the main thing. I feel like I don’t deserve the role, like I’m going to let people down.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about other parts of life too, not just work?

I don’t know… maybe? I mean, work is the big one I notice because it’s right in my face every day. Other stuff, I guess I can get caught up in little things, but I’m not sure I’d call it worrying a lot.

Like, even when I’m at home I’ll start thinking about something work-related, and then I’ll remember I meant to fix this weird router issue—sorry, that’s kind of still work-adjacent, isn’t it. So… yeah, I’m not totally sure. Mostly it feels like the work thing.
Did these feelings start after the change in your role at work?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, it’s hard to pin down exactly because work kind of bleeds into everything, you know? But the noticeable… like, up-and-down pattern, that really started maybe about a month ago, after they asked me to cover the senior analyst duties.

Before that I’d get stressed, sure, like anybody, but this felt more obvious after the role change.
Do these feelings mostly happen when you’re thinking about work or being at work?

Mostly, yeah. It’s tied to work, or even just thinking about work. Like I’ll be sitting there at home and suddenly I’m back in my head going, “Why did they trust me with senior stuff?” and convincing myself I somehow fooled everyone.

It’s not even always something happening right that second… it’s more like I start beating myself up that I’m not really senior material and that I’m going to be found out. Then I’ll spiral off into comparing myself to other people, which is probably not helpful, but yeah—the main trigger seems to be the job and this extra responsibility.
Have these feelings started to interfere with how well you do your job?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m still showing up and getting the work done, so it’s not like I’ve stopped functioning or anything. But I don’t trust myself as much lately, so I keep double-checking things I normally would’ve just finished and moved on from.

And then outside of work… well, I know you asked about the job, but I’ve kind of pulled back from people too. Friends, family. I don’t really feel like being around them when I’m not sure what kind of mood I’m going to be in, or whether my judgment is off. So at work it’s more like I’m slower and second-guessing myself.
Before this role change, did you usually feel this same kind of self-doubt in other situations too?

Not usually in the same way, no. I mean, I’ve had normal doubts before—everybody does, right? Like if I’m fixing something at home and I mess it up, I’ll call myself an idiot for five minutes and then move on.

But this… this is more like I keep coming back to the idea that I’m not really senior material. Like they gave me more responsibility and I somehow fooled them into thinking I could handle it. And then I start replaying things in my head instead of just doing the work. So before the role change, I don’t think it was this constant or this… personal, I guess.
Have you generally avoided social situations because you worry people will judge or reject you?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I mean, I don’t love being judged—who does? But I don’t think I’ve generally avoided people because I’m afraid they’ll reject me.

It’s more… lately with the work stuff, I can get in my own head, and then being around people feels like extra effort. But I don’t know if that’s the same as worrying they’re judging me. I guess I’d have to think about it.
Over the past month, have you been feeling down or depressed much of the time?

Yeah… I think so. Most days lately there’s been this kind of heavy, low feeling. Not always dramatic, exactly, but like I’m going through work and then coming home and everything’s sort of… muted.

It reminds me of when you dim a monitor too far and you can still see what’s on the screen, but it’s all washed out. I don’t know why that’s the example that comes to mind—probably because I stare at screens all day—but that’s kind of how it feels. Like the color’s turned down on everything.
Over the past month, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I think I have. I mean, I usually look forward to little stuff, like grilling on the weekend—messing around with the charcoal, trying not to overcook chicken, that whole thing. Or I’ll go fishing if the weather’s decent. I’ve got records I like putting on, too, old ones I’ve had forever.

Lately, though, the grill just sits there, the fishing stuff is still where I left it, and I’ll look at the records and just… not bother. It’s not like I hate those things now. I just don’t really care enough to start.
Over the past month, has your appetite changed much?

Yeah, a bit. I wouldn’t say it’s some huge thing, but my appetite’s been off. I’ll get home and just grab a few bites of something, or sometimes I’ll skip supper without really deciding to.

It’s funny, because I used to be pretty regular about dinner—nothing fancy, just whatever’s easy. I have this one pan I always use, and it’s been sitting there clean more often than not, which I guess says something. And my belt’s been a little looser, too. I’m not trying to lose weight or anything, it just sort of happened.
Did the low mood start after you took on the senior analyst duties?

Yeah… I think that’s about when it became noticeable. After they asked me to cover the senior analyst stuff, maybe around a month ago, I started realizing things were kind of going up and down more.

At first I thought it was just the workload, you know—new responsibilities, more people asking me questions, all these spreadsheets and old systems nobody documented properly. There’s this one shared folder at work that’s a complete mess, and somehow that became my problem too. But… yeah, the timing lines up. It really started after that.
Have these low mood and loss of interest been present for at least two weeks?

Yeah, I’d say so. It’s been more than two weeks… probably closer to a month, really. It kind of started getting noticeable after they had me cover the senior analyst duties.

I mean, time’s been a little blurry with work stuff—meetings popping up, people asking where files are, and there’s this one reporting thing that never lines up right—but yeah, the low mood and not caring about things has been around at least a couple weeks.
Over the past month, have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty?

Yeah… I guess I have. Maybe “worthless” sounds a little strong, but I’ve been beating myself up a lot.

It’s mostly this thing at work, like… since they gave me those senior duties, I keep thinking I’m not actually senior material. Like I somehow fooled everyone into thinking I could handle more than I really can. And then I’ll make one small mistake or not know where something is in the system, and I’ll just replay it in my head like, “See, you shouldn’t be doing this.”

I mean, there’s this old reporting setup nobody really understands anyway, and half the files are named like someone just mashed the keyboard, so maybe it’s not all me, but… it feels like it is. That’s kind of why I came in, honestly. It’s been hard to shut that off.
Have these mood changes been making it hard for you to take care of things in your daily life?

Yeah… a bit. I mean, I’m still getting to work, so it’s not like everything’s fallen apart or anything. But I’m checking things over and over more than I used to, because I don’t really trust myself lately.

And outside of work, I’ve kind of pulled back. Like if friends or family text, I’ll think, “I should answer that,” and then I just don’t, or I put it off. Part of it is I don’t trust my mood or my judgment right now, and I don’t want to be weird around people. You know, say the wrong thing or make everything awkward.
Do your reaction and distress about the new work role feel stronger than you’d expect for the situation?

Yeah… probably. I mean, I know getting new responsibilities is stressful for anybody, so part of me keeps saying, “Well, of course you’re stressed.” But it feels bigger than that.

I came in because I just keep beating myself up, like I’m not really senior material and I somehow fooled everyone into thinking I can handle more than I actually can. And then I get stuck on that thought.

It’s funny, because the title isn’t even officially changed or anything, it’s just duties, but in my head it’s like this whole… proof that I’m going to get exposed. So yeah, I think my reaction is stronger than it probably should be.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Um… yeah, a little. Not like I’ve sat down and made a plan or anything like that. I haven’t… I haven’t planned to hurt myself.

But I do get these thoughts sometimes, like when I’m lying there in the morning before work, or even after a bad day, where it’s like… maybe it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up. Which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud. I don’t know. I don’t want to scare anybody. It’s more like wanting everything to stop for a while than having some specific thing I’m going to do.
Over the past month, have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah, sleep’s been kind of messed up. Some mornings I wake up way too early and my brain just starts running through client tickets, like stuff I need to fix or what I might’ve missed, and then I can’t get back to sleep.

Other times I technically sleep enough hours, but I still wake up feeling worn out. It’s annoying because then I start doing the math, like, “Well, I got seven hours, so why do I feel like this?” But yeah… over the past month, sleep hasn’t felt restful.
Over the past month, have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions?

I’m… not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I feel distracted a lot, but some of that is just the nature of my job too—there’s always some alert or email or someone asking if I can “just take a quick look” at something, and quick look never means quick.

Making decisions… I don’t know. I guess I notice I’ll stare at something longer than I should, like picking what to respond with, but I don’t know if that’s concentration or just me overthinking. My wife would probably say I do that with dinner too, but that’s been true forever, so… yeah, I’m not sure it’s new exactly.
Over the past month, have you been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual, or feeling so restless that you can’t sit still?

Not slower, I don’t think. If anything it’s kind of the opposite sometimes. Like after work, I’ll get home and I can’t just sit on the couch like a normal person. I start checking servers again, or I’ll notice some little thing around the house and suddenly I’m fixing that, then I’m in the garage looking for a tool, then I remember another thing.

It’s not always productive exactly, it just feels like everything has to be handled right then. My wife will be like, “Can you just sit down for a minute?” and I’m like, yeah, I can, but then I’m up again checking something stupid like whether an update finished. So… restless, yeah, I guess that fits more than moving slow.
Even when you're not thinking about work, do you still feel down?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, work definitely sets me off because there’s always something broken or about to be broken, but even when I’m not actively thinking about that, there’s still this kind of heavy, low feeling.

Like I’ll be home doing normal stuff, and it’s like everything’s just… dulled down. Not dramatic exactly, just most days lately it feels like I’m moving through work and home with the color turned down.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive symptoms are causing clinically significant impairment beyond work stress, which helps distinguish a major depressive episode from an adjustment reaction or occupational problem.
doctor.question: Have these mood changes been making it hard for you to take care of things in your daily life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’m still making it to work, but I’ve had to double-check myself more and I’ve pulled back from friends and family because I don’t trust my mood or my judgment lately.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the mood changes are making daily responsibilities and functioning harder, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… a bit. I mean, I’m still getting to work, so it’s not like everything’s fallen apart or anything. But I’m checking things over and over more than I used to, because I don’t really trust myself lately.

And outside of work, I’ve kind of pulled back. Like if friends or family text, I’ll think, “I should answer that,” and then I just don’t, or I put it off. Part of it is I don’t trust my mood or my judgment right now, and I don’t want to be weird around people. You know, say the wrong thing or make everything awkward.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the symptoms are out of proportion to the work stressor, which helps distinguish adjustment disorder from a mild major depressive episode focused around a stressor.
doctor.question: Do your reaction and distress about the new work role feel stronger than you’d expect for the situation?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I keep beating myself up that I’m not really senior material and that I fooled everyone into thinking I could handle more than I can.
target_item.reason: The question is asking whether the patient's distress and self-blame about the new work role are excessive or stronger than expected, which most directly matches feelings of excessive guilt or worthlessness.

patient.answer:
Yeah… probably. I mean, I know getting new responsibilities is stressful for anybody, so part of me keeps saying, “Well, of course you’re stressed.” But it feels bigger than that.

I came in because I just keep beating myself up, like I’m not really senior material and I somehow fooled everyone into thinking I can handle more than I actually can. And then I get stuck on that thought.

It’s funny, because the title isn’t even officially changed or anything, it’s just duties, but in my head it’s like this whole… proof that I’m going to get exposed. So yeah, I think my reaction is stronger than it probably should be.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has had thoughts of death or self-harm, which is critical for assessing major depressive episode severity and immediate safety.
doctor.question: Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself, but I do catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up some morning.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is directly asking about thoughts that life is not worth living or self-harm, which corresponds to recurrent thoughts of death or suicidal ideation.

patient.answer:
Um… yeah, a little. Not like I’ve sat down and made a plan or anything like that. I haven’t… I haven’t planned to hurt myself.

But I do get these thoughts sometimes, like when I’m lying there in the morning before work, or even after a bad day, where it’s like… maybe it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up. Which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud. I don’t know. I don’t want to scare anybody. It’s more like wanting everything to stop for a while than having some specific thing I’m going to do.

inference.note: Added F32.1 because the patient now endorses a >2-week depressive episode with depressed mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, guilt/worthlessness, functional impairment, and passive death wishes; this makes major depressive episode more likely and at least moderate in severity. Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood remains possible given clear temporal link to work stressor. F41.1 is less likely because symptoms are largely work-related rather than pervasive across domains.

doctor.intent: Assess whether there is a neurovegetative symptom of major depression that would help distinguish a major depressive episode from adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood.
doctor.question: Over the past month, have you been having trouble sleeping?

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: Now I either wake up way too early thinking about client tickets and can’t get back to sleep, or I sleep enough hours and still feel worn out.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about trouble sleeping over the past month, which matches sleep disturbance.

patient.answer:
Yeah, sleep’s been kind of messed up. Some mornings I wake up way too early and my brain just starts running through client tickets, like stuff I need to fix or what I might’ve missed, and then I can’t get back to sleep.

Other times I technically sleep enough hours, but I still wake up feeling worn out. It’s annoying because then I start doing the math, like, “Well, I got seven hours, so why do I feel like this?” But yeah… over the past month, sleep hasn’t felt restful.

inference.note: Added sleep disturbance and passive death wishes, further supporting a major depressive episode. Generalized anxiety disorder is less likely because symptoms are predominantly triggered by the work role change rather than excessive anxiety across multiple domains. Z56.9 is not needed as a primary diagnostic candidate given clearer syndromal diagnoses.

doctor.intent: Determine whether impaired concentration/indecisiveness is present as an additional major depressive symptom to distinguish a major depressive episode from adjustment disorder with depressed mood/anxiety.
doctor.question: Over the past month, have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about trouble concentrating or making decisions, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific item for concentration problems or indecisiveness.

patient.answer:
I’m… not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I feel distracted a lot, but some of that is just the nature of my job too—there’s always some alert or email or someone asking if I can “just take a quick look” at something, and quick look never means quick.

Making decisions… I don’t know. I guess I notice I’ll stare at something longer than I should, like picking what to respond with, but I don’t know if that’s concentration or just me overthinking. My wife would probably say I do that with dinner too, but that’s been true forever, so… yeah, I’m not sure it’s new exactly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether psychomotor retardation or agitation is present to clarify if the patient meets full criteria for a major depressive episode rather than adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood.
doctor.question: Over the past month, have you been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual, or feeling so restless that you can’t sit still?

target_item.name: Increased_Activity
target_item.manifestation: During that same stretch I couldn’t sit still after work and kept jumping into server checks, home projects, and little fixes around the house like everything had to be handled right then.
target_item.reason: The question asks about psychomotor restlessness or being unable to sit still, which most closely matches the profile describing periods of increased activity and not being able to sit still.

patient.answer:
Not slower, I don’t think. If anything it’s kind of the opposite sometimes. Like after work, I’ll get home and I can’t just sit on the couch like a normal person. I start checking servers again, or I’ll notice some little thing around the house and suddenly I’m fixing that, then I’m in the garage looking for a tool, then I remember another thing.

It’s not always productive exactly, it just feels like everything has to be handled right then. My wife will be like, “Can you just sit down for a minute?” and I’m like, yeah, I can, but then I’m up again checking something stupid like whether an update finished. So… restless, yeah, I guess that fits more than moving slow.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive symptoms are confined to the identifiable work stressor or occur independently, to distinguish major depressive episode from adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood.
doctor.question: Even when you're not thinking about work, do you still feel down?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days lately I’ve had this heavy, low feeling, like I’m just moving through work and home with the color turned down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the low mood persists even outside work-related thoughts, which directly matches depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I mean, work definitely sets me off because there’s always something broken or about to be broken, but even when I’m not actively thinking about that, there’s still this kind of heavy, low feeling.

Like I’ll be home doing normal stuff, and it’s like everything’s just… dulled down. Not dramatic exactly, just most days lately it feels like I’m moving through work and home with the color turned down.

opening_question.intent: Elicit the patient's chief complaint to begin narrowing the possible diagnosis
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a moderate depressive episode: persistent depressed mood and anhedonia for about 1 month, along with appetite/weight loss, sleep disturbance, feelings of worthlessness/excessive guilt, passive death wishes, psychomotor restlessness, and functional decline. Although symptoms began after a work-role stressor and adjustment disorder was considered, the syndrome is pervasive beyond the immediate stress context and fulfills a full depressive episode, making F32.1 the better fit.
